title: Feasibility of a Mindfulness and Physical Activity Promotion Intervention After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction
official: Mind in Motion: Determining the Feasibility of a Mindfulness and Physical Activity Promotion Intervention After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a 6-week mobile-delivered intervention combining mindfulness meditation (Headspace) and personalized, wearable-derived physical activity goals (Oura Ring) can be feasibly delivered to young people who are 1-5 years post-anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and who have elevated fear of reinjury. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can the Mind in Motion intervention be implemented with acceptable rates of recruitment, retention, engagement (mindfulness session completion, Oura Ring wear), and participant-rated acceptability?
* On days following a completed mindfulness session, do participants report lower anticipated fear of movement and show higher objectively measured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), compared with other days?

Participants will:

* Complete two brief in-person visits (approximately 1 week apart) that frame a 6-week home-based intervention period, followed by a remote assessment 4 weeks after the intervention ends.
* Wear a research-grade activPAL accelerometer on the thigh for 7 days before and 7 days after the intervention to measure objective physical activity.
* During the 6-week intervention, complete five 10-minute Headspace mindfulness sessions per week, wear an Oura Ring daily to receive personalized daily activity goals, and complete brief twice-daily check-ins (ecological momentary assessments) about fear, mood, and activity.
* Complete standard questionnaires about injury-related fear, psychological readiness for activity, and knee function/symptoms at baseline, mid-intervention, immediately after the intervention, and at a 4-week follow-up.
* Complete a brief audio-recorded exit interview describing their experience with the intervention.

This is a single-arm, single-site feasibility study; there is no control group and no randomization. Findings will inform the design of a future multisite randomized controlled trial.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 15-30 years old
* Undergone primary, unilateral anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR)
* 1-5 years post-ACLR at enrollment
* Elevated injury-related fear at baseline, defined as a score of 17 or greater on the Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia-11 (TSK-11)
* Self-reported reduction in physical activity since ACLR, as confirmed through the ACL-RETURN survey administered during prescreening
* Medically cleared for physical activity participation
* Willing and able to wear an Oura Ring daily for 6 weeks
* Willing and able to complete mindfulness sessions delivered through the Mind in Motion mobile application using the Headspace platform
* Access to a smartphone compatible with the Mind in Motion application and the Oura application
* Able to read and understand English
* Willingness and ability to comply with all scheduled visits and study procedures

Exclusion Criteria:

* ACL reconstruction performed more than 5 years or less than 1 year prior to enrollment
* Concomitant ligamentous or articular cartilage procedures at the time of ACLR that limit physical activity participation
* Any other lower extremity injury or condition that currently limits participation in physical activity
* Current medical condition that restricts physical activity participation
* Diagnosis of any form of arthritis
* Suspected or confirmed pregnancy
* Prisoners
* Cognitively impaired individuals
* Non-English speaking
